'''Indian Oil Corporation Limited''' ('''IOCL'''), ([[d/b/a]] '''Indian Oil''') is an Indian [[multinational company|multinational]]<ref>{{cite press release|quote=TEL AVIV, Israel, Feb. 14, 2024 /PRNewswire/ -- Phinergy (TASE: PNRG) - which develops metal-air technology that produces electricity by combining oxygen from the air with metals - is delighted to announce that multinational energy giant, Indian Oil Corporation, has completed its second round of investment in the company in the amount of $12.5 million.|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/in/news-releases/indian-oil-corporation-completes-second-round-of-investment-in-phinergy-bringing-its-holding-in-the-company-to-17-302061630.html|title=Indian Oil Corporation completes second round of investment in Phinergy, bringing its holding in the company to 17%|website=PR Newswire}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|quote=Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), established in 1959 and headquartered in New Delhi, India, is a multinational that explores and produces petroleum products and is also a manufacturer of petrochemicals.|url=https://us.metoree.com/companies/191532/|title=Indian Oil Corporation Ltd - Company Profile and Products|website=Metoree}}</ref> [[Oil and gas industry in India|oil and gas]] company under the [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|ownership]] of the [[Government of India]] and administrative control of the [[Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas]]. It is a [[Public sector undertakings in India|public sector undertaking]] which is [[Registered office|registered]] in [[Mumbai]] and headquartered in [[New Delhi]].<ref name="arpt2018">{{cite book |title=Annual report 2017-2018 |publisher=Indian Oil Corporation |location=Mumbai |url=https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/notification/PDFs/71APDIR030215.pdf |access-date=11 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018140037/https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/Notification/PDFs/71APDIR030215.pdf |archive-date=18 October 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> It is the largest [[Public sector undertakings in India|government-owned oil producer]]<ref>{{Cite book |author1=Lee, Mordecai |author2=Neeley, Grant |author3=Stewart, Kendra B. |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/1263816753 |title=The practice of government public relations |date=20 July 2021 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-39496-2 |oclc=1263816753 |access-date=8 May 2022 |archive-date=8 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220508103925/https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/1263816753 |url-status=live }}</ref> in the country both in terms of capacity and revenue. It has consolidated refining capacity of 80.55MMTPA.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iocl.com/MediaDetails/48582#:~:text=IndianOil%20in%20Media&text=India%20plans%20to%20raise%20its,government%20report%20said%20on%20Thursday.|title=India plans 77% rise in refining capacity by 2030}}</ref>

Indian Oil's business interests overlap the entire [[hydrocarbon]] [[value chain]], including [[refining]], [[pipeline]], marketing of [[petroleum product]]s, [[Hydrocarbon exploration|exploration]] and [[Extraction of petroleum|production]] of [[Petroleum]], [[Natural gas vehicle|natural gas]] and [[petrochemical]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=IOC stock page. |url=https://www.reuters.com/finance/stocks/companyProfile/IOC.NS |access-date=17 September 2017 |website=Reuters |language=en-US}}</ref> Indian Oil has ventured into [[renewable energy]] and globalisation of downstream operations. It has subsidiaries in [[Sri Lanka]] ([[Lanka IOC]]),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iocl.com/AboutUs/GroupCompanies(LIOC).aspx|title=IndianOil Corporation {{!}} Lanka IOC PLC|website=www.iocl.com|access-date=17 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916142148/https://www.iocl.com/AboutUs/GroupCompanies(LIOC).aspx|archive-date=16 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Mauritius]] (IndianOil (Mauritius) Ltd),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iocl.com/AboutUs/GroupCompanies(Mauritius).aspx|title=IndianOil Corporation {{!}} IndianOil (Mauritius) Ltd.|website=www.iocl.com|access-date=17 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916141726/https://www.iocl.com/AboutUs/GroupCompanies(Mauritius).aspx|archive-date=16 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> and the [[Middle East]] (IOC Middle East FZE).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iocl.com/AboutUs/GroupCompanies(MiddleEast).aspx|title=IndianOil Corporation {{!}} Group Companies|website=www.iocl.com|access-date=17 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916142400/https://www.iocl.com/AboutUs/GroupCompanies(MiddleEast).aspx|archive-date=16 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

Indian Oil is ranked 94th on the [[Fortune Global 500]] list of the world's biggest corporations as of 2022.<ref name="fortune">{{cite news | url=https://fortune.com/company/indian-oil/global500/ | title=Fortune Global 500 list | access-date=10 August 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190807080136/https://fortune.com/global500/2019/ | archive-date=7 August 2019 | url-status=live }}</ref> As of 31 March 2021, Indian Oil has 31,648 employees, out of which 17,762 are executives and 13,876 non-executives, while 2,776 are women.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Annual Report 2020-21|title=Financial Performance : Oil and Energy News|url=https://iocl.com/pages/financial-performance-overview|access-date=2021-09-03|website=iocl.com|archive-date=3 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903125250/https://iocl.com/pages/financial-performance-overview|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Indian Oil Corporation Ltd Management Discussions|url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/indian-oil-corporation-ltd/management-discussions/12002|access-date=27 May 2021|website=IIFL Securities|archive-date=13 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613062703/https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/indian-oil-corporation-ltd/management-discussions/12002|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Annual Report 2019-20|url=https://www.iocl.com/download/IndianOil-Annual-Report-2019-20.pdf|access-date=27 May 2021|website=IOC - official website|publisher=Indian oil corporation|archive-date=13 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613062710/https://iocl.com/download/IndianOil-Annual-Report-2019-20.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

== History ==
In May 2018, IOCL became India's most profitable [[Government of India Act 1935|government corporation]] for the second consecutive year, with a record profit of ₹21,346 crores in 2017–18.<ref>{{cite news |title=IOC most profitable PSU for 2nd yr in a row; displaces ONGC |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/pti-feed/story/ioc-most-profitable-psu-for-2nd-yr-in-a-row-displaces-ongc-1246700-2018-05-31 |publisher=[[India Today]] |date=31 May 2018 |access-date=31 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180606074512/https://www.indiatoday.in/pti-feed/story/ioc-most-profitable-psu-for-2nd-yr-in-a-row-displaces-ongc-1246700-2018-05-31 |archive-date=6 June 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2020, the company signed a deal with the Russian oil company [[Rosneft]] to buy 140,000 barrels per day of crude in year 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-oil-russia-idUSKBN1ZZ1CD|title=India's IOC signs annual deal on option to buy crude from Russia's Rosneft|date=5 February 2020|work=Reuters|access-date=5 February 2020|language=en|archive-date=5 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205132008/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-oil-russia-idUSKBN1ZZ1CD|url-status=live}}</ref> By 1 April 2020, IndianOil was in absolute readiness to launch [[Bharat stage emission standards|BS-VI (Bharat Stage VI)]] fuels in all its retail outlets in [[Telangana]] and adopt world-class emission norms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/indian-oil-to-supply-bs-vi-fuels-in-telangana-from-april-1-11583985429610.html|title=Indian Oil to supply BS-VI fuels in Telangana from April 1|date=12 March 2020|website=mint|access-date=12 March 2020|archive-date=13 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613062701/https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/indian-oil-to-supply-bs-vi-fuels-in-telangana-from-april-1-11583985429610.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In January 2021, sales were registered at an all-time high of 410,000 barrels of oil per day till 26 January 2021. [[Delek]], [[QatarEnergy]], and [[Saudi Aramco]] are its largest business partners, with [[Abu Dhabi National Oil Company]] and [[National Iranian Oil Company]] signing deals to deliver high production output by the end of 2020.

In March 2022, [[Apollo Hospitals]] replaced Indian Oil Corporation in [[NIFTY 50|Nifty 50]] benchmark index.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/nse-revises-its-eligibility-criteria-and-replaces-stocks-in-its-key-indices-8160991.html | title=Apollo Hospitals replaces IOC in Nifty50 as NSE revises eligibility norms, swaps stocks in key indices | date=24 February 2022 | access-date=27 June 2022 | archive-date=27 June 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627074348/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/nse-revises-its-eligibility-criteria-and-replaces-stocks-in-its-key-indices-8160991.html | url-status=live }}</ref>

== Controversy ==

=== Indian Oil Corporation's activities in Russia ===
Indian Oil Corporation has faced criticism for continuing its operations in Russia despite widespread international sanctions imposed after [[Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022]]. The corporation has been listed on platforms such as ''Leave Russia,'' which monitors companies still active in the country, raising ethical concerns about its stance in the global effort to economically isolate Russia. Critics argue that such actions undermine international solidarity against the invasion of Ukraine. The company's activities have sparked questions about its commitment to corporate social responsibility and its alignment with international norms during geopolitical crises.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Oil Corporation |url=https://leave-russia.org/indian-oil-corporation |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=leave-russia.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=India signs long-term oil deals with Russia despite sanctions |url=https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2024/10/22/7480866/ |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=Pravda.com.ua |language=en}}</ref>

=== Products and services ===

Indian Oil accounts for nearly half of India's petroleum products market share, 35% national refining capacity (together with its subsidiary [[Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited|Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd.]] or CPCL), and 71% downstream sector pipelines through capacity. The Indian Oil Group owns and operates 11 of India's 23 <ref>{{cite news |title=India Oil Corporation nears first deal to export fuel to Bangladesh: Sources |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/india-oil-corporation-nears-first-deal-to-export-fuel-to-bangladesh-sources/article31614027.ece |work=@businessline |language=en |access-date=22 May 2020 |archive-date=23 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200523131510/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/india-oil-corporation-nears-first-deal-to-export-fuel-to-bangladesh-sources/article31614027.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> refineries with a combined refining capacity of 80.7 million [[tonne]]s per year.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pipeline-conference.com/companies/indian-oil-corporation|title=Indian Oil Corporation|date=3 July 2011|work=13th Pipeline Technology Conference|access-date=17 September 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918154418/https://www.pipeline-conference.com/companies/indian-oil-corporation|archive-date=18 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Indian Oil's cross-country pipeline network, for the transport of crude oil to refineries and finished products to high-demand centres, spans over 13,000 km. The company has a throughput capacity of 80.49 million tonnes per year for crude oil and petroleum products and 9.5 million cubic metres per day at [[Standard temperature and pressure|standard conditions]] for gas. On 19 November 2017, IOCL, in collaboration with [[Ola Cabs|Ola]], launched India's first electric charging station at one of its petrol-diesel stations in Nagpur.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/indian-oil-sets-up-indias-first-electric-vehicle-charging-station/article9969318.ece|title=Indian Oil sets up India's first electric vehicle charging station|date=22 November 2017|work=The Hindu BusinessLine|access-date=23 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122070718/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/indian-oil-sets-up-indias-first-electric-vehicle-charging-station/article9969318.ece|archive-date=22 November 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Indian governments' National Electric Mobility Mission Plan launched in 2013 aims at gradually ensuring a vehicle population of 6 to 8 million electric and hybrid vehicles in India by 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=National Electric Mobility Mission Plan|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=116719|website=Government of India Press Information Bureau|access-date=17 March 2018|date=10 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317232413/http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=116719|archive-date=17 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Servo is the lubricants brand under which IOCL operates its lubricant business. Servo is the largest selling lubricant brand in both automotive and industrial segments.

It is said that deals with [[Royal Dutch Shell]] and [[Surgutneftegas]] and [[Chevron Corporation]] have been signed for exclusive business plans for supply in Asia with the [[Indian Oil Company]], which are worth 20 billion dollars per year.

== Listing and shareholding ==

Indian Oil's [[Common stock|equity shares]] are listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and [[National Stock Exchange of India]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/indian-oil-corporation-ltd/infocompanylisting/companyid-11924.cms |title=Listing Information – Indian Oil Corporation Limited |publisher=Economic Times |access-date=27 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140227185053/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/indian-oil-corporation-ltd/infocompanylisting/companyid-11924.cms |archive-date=27 February 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As of September 2018, it was owned 51% by the Government of India (through the [[President of India]]), and 43% by other entities. The latter included corporate bodies (20%), [[ONGC]] (14%), [[Life Insurance Corporation|LIC]] (6%), Foreign portfolio investors (6%),<ref name="arpt2018" /> [[Oil India Limited]] (5%) and [[ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund|Indian Mutual funds]] (4%).<ref>{{cite web |title=Share holding pattern 30 September 2018 |url=https://iocl.com/download/LODR-SHP(2018-09-30).pdf |website=IOC Official website |publisher=IOC |access-date=11 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011133503/https://iocl.com/download/LODR-SHP(2018-09-30).pdf |archive-date=11 October 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

This was similar to its shareholding in 2017. As of 31 December 2017, the [[Corporate promoter|Promoters]] [[Government of India]] held approx. 56.98% of the shares in Indian Oil Corporation. The public held the rest of the shares – 43.02%. This includes Mutual Fund Companies, Foreign Portfolio Investors, Financial Institutions/ Banks, Insurance Companies, Individual Shareholders and Trusts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iocl.com/download/LODRSHP-(2017-12-31).pdf|title=Indian Oil Corporation {{!}} Shareholding Pattern|date=31 December 2017|website=www.iocl.com|access-date=25 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225205537/https://www.iocl.com/download/LODRSHP-(2017-12-31).pdf|archive-date=25 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> IOCL's Market cap as of December 2022 was Rs. 1,10,075.05 crore.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Top 100 stocks by Market Capitalization {{!}} BSE Listed stocks Market Capitalization |url=https://www.bseindia.com/markets/equity/eqreports/topmarketcapitalization.aspx |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=www.bseindia.com |archive-date=25 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725202033/https://www.bseindia.com/markets/equity/EQReports/TopMarketCapitalization.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Strategic partnerships ==
=== IOC Phinergy Pvt Ltd ===
Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) buys a stake in [[Phinergy]] ([[Israel]]) for manufacturing, development, and sale of [[Aluminium-air batteries|aluminum-air batteries]] (Al-Air batteries) for [[electric vehicle]]s. This joint venture is ready to facilitate the development of Al-Air technology by intending to set up a factory in India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/oil-and-gas/indianoil-buys-stake-in-phinergy-of-israel-for-manufacturing-of-aluminium-air-batteries/73935714|title=IndianOil buys stake in Phinergy of Israel for manufacturing of aluminium-air batteries - ET EnergyWorld|website=ETEnergyworld.com|access-date=13 March 2020|archive-date=6 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200306133310/https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/oil-and-gas/indianoil-buys-stake-in-phinergy-of-israel-for-manufacturing-of-aluminium-air-batteries/73935714|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Competition ==
Indian Oil Corporation has two major domestic competitors – [[Bharat Petroleum]] and [[Hindustan Petroleum]] – and both are state-controlled, like Indian Oil Corporation. Major private competitors include – [[Reliance Petroleum]], [[Essar Oil, Now renamed as Nayara|Nayara Energy]] and [[Royal Dutch Shell|Shell]].

== Oil Industry Development Board ==
India has begun the development of a strategic crude oil reserve sized at {{convert|37.4|Moilbbl|m3}}, enough for three weeks of consumption.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gasandoil.com/goc/news/nts43834.htm |title=Alexander's Gas & Oil Connections – India to build up storage of crude oil |publisher=Gasandoil.com |date=21 September 2004 |access-date=26 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418001150/http://www.gasandoil.com/goc/news/nts43834.htm |archive-date=18 April 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Petroleum stocks have been transferred from the Indian Oil Corporation to the Oil Industry Development Board (OIDB).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2006/04/02/stories/2006040202220200.htm |title=Strategic oil reserves to come directly under Govt |publisher=The Hindu Business Line |date=2 April 2006 |access-date=26 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090212181220/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2006/04/02/stories/2006040202220200.htm |archive-date=12 February 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> The OIDB then created the [[Strategic Petroleum Reserve (India)|Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd (ISPRL)]] to serve as the controlling government agency for the strategic reserve.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/India_to_form_crude_oil_reserve_of_5_mmt/articleshow/2137148.cms |title='India to form crude oil reserve of 5 mmt'- Oil & Gas-Energy-News By Industry-News-The Economic Times |publisher=Economictimes.indiatimes.com |date=20 June 2007 |access-date=26 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090111113327/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/India_to_form_crude_oil_reserve_of_5_mmt/articleshow/2137148.cms |archive-date=11 January 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref>

extract:
Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), (d/b/a Indian Oil) is an Indian multinational oil and gas company under the ownership of the Government of India and administrative control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. It is a public sector undertaking which is registered in Mumbai and headquartered in New Delhi. It is the largest government-owned oil producer in the country both in terms of capacity and revenue. It has consolidated refining capacity of 80.55MMTPA.
Indian Oil's business interests overlap the entire hydrocarbon value chain, including refining, pipeline, marketing of petroleum products, exploration and production of Petroleum, natural gas and petrochemicals. Indian Oil has ventured into renewable energy and globalisation of downstream operations. It has subsidiaries in Sri Lanka (Lanka IOC), Mauritius (IndianOil (Mauritius) Ltd), and the Middle East (IOC Middle East FZE).
Indian Oil is ranked 94th on the Fortune Global 500 list of the world's biggest corporations as of 2022. As of 31 March 2021, Indian Oil has 31,648 employees, out of which 17,762 are executives and 13,876 non-executives, while 2,776 are women.
